commit_subject: Address West Virginia resident core review
description: Independent review found unsupported-profile intermediate exposure, incomplete SS/exemption/gambling/full-year proofs, withdrawal addback semantics, and missing boundary/branch tests.

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The low-income earned-income exclusion returned a nonzero deduction for any return meeting the AGI thresholds, omitting W. Va. Code 11-21-10(d), which bars the exclusion for a taxable year covering a period of less than twelve months; the fix wraps the whole formula in `if wv_pit_2026_is_full_year_resident_return: ... else: 0`.
triage.triage_notes: Provision WAS read: resolve_provision.py on us-wv/statute/11-21-10 returns subsection (d) verbatim -- 'Taxable year must be full taxable year. -- Except in the case of a taxable year closed by reason of the death of the taxpayer, no credit shall be allowed under this section in the case of a taxable year covering a period of less than twelve months.' Pre-fix, `wv_pit_2026_is_full_year_resident_return` appeared ONLY in the wv_pit_2026_supported_profile_applies gate (parent line 220), never in the exclusion rule's own formula, and the exclusion rule was not private, so reading it directly for a short taxable year produced a wrong nonzero amount. Caveat on the fix: it does not implement the (d) death-of-taxpayer carve-out (a short year closed by death still gets zero); the module fails closed outside the full-year profile, so this is under- rather than over-claiming. The commit consists of four distinct change classes bundled together -- (1) the full-year gate above (fidelity); (2) renaming four increasing-modification withdrawal inputs to `..._not_in_federal_adjusted_gross_income` with matching descriptions and a new module-description sentence 'Increasing-modification withdrawal inputs are expressly limited to amounts not already included in federal adjusted gross income.', which aligns the inputs with the 11-21-12(b) lead-in 'There shall be added to federal adjusted gross income, unless already included therein' already cited as a pre-existing proof atom -- a second, weaker unrepresented_clause signal implemented only as input rename/description, with formulas otherwise unchanged; (3) adding `private: true` to eight intermediate rules, an output-surface narrowing that removes exposure the module arguably never intended to claim (not itself a defect under the task's 'added scope' rule, and it removes rather than adds surface); (4) five added proof-atom excerpts (social security pre/post-2026 AGI conditions, 11-21-9 gambling and personal-exemption definitions, 11-21-10 full-year condition on the profile gate) -- pure provenance, mechanical. Confidence held below 0.8 because the commit body is empty and the PR body names the finding set generically ('full-year proofs', 'withdrawal addback semantics') rather than stating the formula defect; the diff plus the resolved statute make the kind clear. Also changed outside this module index: the companion test file and the encoding manifest. No follow-up commits inspected.
triage.verifier_justification: I tried to refute this as mere hardening and could not: the pinned corpus text of W. Va. Code §11-21-10(d) reads "Taxable year must be full taxable year. -- Except in the case of a taxable year closed by reason of the death of the taxpayer, no credit shall be allowed under this section in the case of a taxable year covering a period of less than twelve months", and the pre-fix `wv_pit_2026_low_income_earned_income_exclusion` formula tested only filing status and the AGI thresholds, so it returned a nonzero deduction on a short taxable year. The fix wraps the entire formula in `if wv_pit_2026_is_full_year_resident_return: ... else: 0` and adds a proof atom quoting that subsection, i.e. it adds a source-stated clause the encoding omitted. The rule was public before this commit (`private: true` is added in the same hunk) and the companion test now asserts `is_full_year_resident_return: false` → exclusion `'0'`, so the omission was observable at the module's output surface rather than masked by the `wv_pit_2026_supported_profile_applies` gate. Kind unrepresented_clause fits better than wrong_entity_or_scope because the decisive change at the cited rule_path is a missing statutory condition added to the formula, not a re-scoping of the population.

triage.verifier_notes:
Verification path: corpus release us-rulespec-2026-07-22-current-la-status-fix, provision us-wv/statute/11-21-10, body sha256 9dd6bea…858fbe; the added proof-atom excerpt is verbatim from subsection (d).

Three caveats for the reviewer, none of which overturn the verdict:
1. The fix over-corrects relative to the source. §11-21-10(d) excepts "a taxable year closed by reason of the death of the taxpayer", but the new gate denies the exclusion for every non-full-year return with no death carve-out. The module fails closed in a case the statute allows; that is a residual (opposite-direction) fidelity gap in the post state, not a reason to reject the pre-state as wrong.
2. The gate input `wv_pit_2026_is_full_year_resident_return` is described as "Whether the return covers a full taxable year for West Virginia full-year residents", conflating residency status with the twelve-month period test that (d) actually states.
3. The commit is mixed, so the other rule_names in this candidate carry changes of different character: `wv_pit_2026_input_domain_is_valid`, `wv_pit_2026_supported_profile_applies`, and `wv_pit_2026_profile_candidate_additions` change only through the rename of four withdrawal inputs to `..._not_in_federal_adjusted_gross_income` (a separate narrowing of increasing-modification semantics that would need its own §11-21-12(b) check), plus `private: true` metadata on intermediates and added proof atoms (provenance/scope hardening). The first reader's quote is the PR's generic laundry-list review sentence and does not by itself evidence this kind; the diff line and the §11-21-10(d) text do.
